tasks.title: Stall speed
tasks.solution: V_s = √(2·m·g/(ρ·S·C_L,max)), with S in m² (dm² ÷ 100). Choose a cruise speed 1.3–1.5 times higher.

tasks.title: Wing loading
tasks.solution: W/S = m/S. Below 30 g/dm² is a slow trainer; 60–100 is a fast wing with a hard landing.

tasks.title: EAS and true airspeed
tasks.solution: Lift depends on dynamic pressure, so the stall is constant in EAS. TAS = EAS·√(ρ₀/ρ), ρ₀ = 1.225; this is how TECS multiplies AIRSPEED_MIN by EAS2TAS (AP_TECS.cpp:420). The module's example: 8.53 m/s at ρ = 1.058 (1500 m) → 9.18 m/s.

tasks.title: STALL_PREVENTION roll limit
tasks.solution: n_max = (V/V_s)² = k², roll ≤ arccos(1/n_max) (Attitude.cpp:723–746); the firmware does not lower the limit below 25° without FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 16. The module's example: V = 10, AIRSPEED_STALL = 8.5 → k = 1.176 → 43.7°.

tasks.title: Trading speed for altitude
tasks.solution: The TECS specific energies: SKE = ½V², SPE = g·h. Δh = (v₁² − v₂²)/(2g). The module's example: 12 → 10 m/s gives 2.24 m, which is how much altitude the wing gives up or takes when TECS redistributes energy with pitch.
